The earlier grading/reference uncertainty is resolved for the ordinary A∞ intrinsic-formality criterion actually asserted. [Kadeishvili, §2 and Corollary 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210331) uses cochains of arity n and internal degree 2−n, and concludes that every minimal higher structure with the given binary product is equivalent to the trivial higher structure. [Keller §§3.1, 3.3 and 3.5](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bernhard.keller/publ/ioan.pdf) explicitly separates ordinary A∞ algebras from the subsequent strict-unital theory.

In the [actual vanishing predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/IntrinsicFormality/Criterion.lean#L80), a suspended degree-q cochain of arity n has original internal degree q+1−n. Thus its degree-one arity-n cocycle has degree 2−n, as does the degree-zero arity-(n−1) primitive. The [differential](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Hochschild/Basic.lean#L73) is the graded bracket with the binary multiplication; the [proved arity identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Obstruction.lean#L205) confirms that it raises arity by one. Positive tensor lengths omit arity zero, which does not affect the cocycles and boundaries used for n≥3. This is not normalized cohomology obtained by quotienting out a unit.

The [conclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/IntrinsicFormality.lean#L80) quantifies over all A∞ algebras with the prescribed cohomology algebra and concludes ordinary formality; it does not promise a unit-preserving equivalence. Therefore the theorem is a correctly scoped ordinary criterion, while the roadmap's additional strict-unital normalization remains an enhancement, not a hidden hypothesis or claimed conclusion here. The [roadmap acceptance table](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/DGAInfinity/README.md#L677) explicitly assigns the exterior/quiver transfer examples to Layer 3, not this Layer 8 criterion; my previous review overextended those checks. No separate intrinsic-formality Check is prescribed there. The actual [degree-zero intrinsic-formality theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/IntrinsicFormality.lean#L182) supplies a nonvacuous boundary calibration. Inspected proofs have no sorry; this update records source and primary-reference verification, not a fresh build.

Correctly stated. The previous reference gap is resolved by [Jørgensen's own 1979 paper, Proposition 1 and its discussion on pp.90–91](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/6BDE9DE2806F4A5B5744938995A7EE85/S0008414X0001141Xa.pdf/div-class-title-comments-on-a-discreteness-condition-for-subgroups-of-sl-2-c-div.pdf): the trace inequality holds for discrete non-elementary pairs, with exceptional elementary pairs preserving the first element's fixed-point set. Its `tr(A²)−2` equals `(tr A)²−4` for determinant-one matrices. For real elliptic A, a real orientation-preserving Möbius map preserving its conjugate fixed-point pair must fix the upper-half-plane point; the stabilizer is abelian, giving precisely the project's projective-commutation exception. Alternatively the only noncyclic elementary Fuchsian case has elliptic half-turns, whose trace is zero and first absolute-value term is already 4. Thus no non-elementarity assumption was accidentally dropped.

The [pinned theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Fuchsian/Jorgensen.lean#L418) uses genuine SL₂(ℝ) lifts in a discrete PSL₂(ℝ) subgroup, the strict elliptic condition, and the standard commutator order. Both sides and the exception are unchanged by lift signs; ±I fail ellipticity. The [commutator-displacement formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/Displacement.lean#L171) checks the constants independently of the inequality: its left side becomes `(4−tr²A)(1+cosh d)/2`. The [geometric form](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Fuchsian/Jorgensen.lean#L404) agrees by the half-angle identity. These source witnesses are proved without sorry.

Rechecking the human target resolves the previous scope uncertainty: [Layer15 item5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L1743) explicitly asks for geodesics of the general measured-kernel quotient, using a selector relative to the optimal endpoint law when no Borel bicombing is given. It is not required to identify these quotient geodesics, and imposing it here conflated two targets.

The [pinned instance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Geodesic.lean#L236) and [carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Space.lean#L45) match [BMNN Theorem45](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume26/24-2189/24-2189.pdf): standard-Borel probability carriers, strongly measurable finite-p-moment Z-valued kernels, and complete separable geodesic Z. The no-½ normalization rescales lengths uniformly. The range `1≤p≤∞` is supported by the Lp interpolation bound, including the essential-supremum endpoint. The construction uses an optimal coupling and its product-pushforward law to obtain measurable target paths; it makes no unjustified global Borel-selection claim. Quotient choices therefore affect representatives, not the asserted existence of a segment.

Results for all [shared acceptance items](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L1833): measure-preserving pullback gives zero ([Basic379](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Basic.lean#L379)); zero iff weak kernel isomorphism passes ([Zero85](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Zero.lean#L85)), while the additional metric-isometry converse remains unlocated and belongs to item4. Singleton-Lp normalization passes ([Basic484](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Basic.lean#L484)); the exact uniform two-point formula passes for finite p and infinity ([TwoPoint91](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/TwoPoint.lean#L91)); explicit gluing establishes the triangle check ([Basic449](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Basic.lean#L449)); the four-index finite objective agrees with generic GW ([Finite124](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Finite.lean#L124)). These proved witnesses calibrate the distance used here and contain no sorry.

Correctly stated as the vector-field Fréchet subdifferential. The earlier all-optimal-versus-infimum concern is resolved by a comparison with [AGS2005, Proposition8.5.4 and (10.3.13)](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~sayan/ambrosio.pdf). Here is the additional argument, rather than an assumed equivalence. Project ξ orthogonally onto the L²-closure of smooth cylindrical gradients. The discarded divergence-free component pairs to zero with every optimal displacement by Proposition8.5.4. For a smooth cylindrical f, Taylor's formula and equal marginals bound the difference of its pairings along two optimal plans by `||D²f||∞ W₂²`. Approximating the tangent projection by ∇f changes each pairing by at most `||ξ_tan−∇f||₂ W₂`. Consequently the difference is uniformly `o(W₂)`. Taking an infimum or requiring every optimal plan therefore gives the same first-order inequality for vector fields, even at singular laws. This does not identify the definition with the distinct extended plan or all-coupling strong notions.

The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Subdifferential.lean#L106) uses the actual P₂ carrier and L² classes, excludes both infinite energies at μ, and uses the W₂ neighborhood with the correct negative ε-error. Marginal preservation and Cauchy–Schwarz give representative independence and integrability. Optimal plans exist under the complete separable hypotheses, so the quantifier is not vacuous; at ν=μ its displacement vanishes.

Checks for [Layer11.4's subdifferential component](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L1267) pass in source without sorry: [convexity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Subdifferential.lean#L133), [closedness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Subdifferential.lean#L155), [minimal selection when nonempty](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Subdifferential.lean#L175), and [the gradient of a strongly convex potential with linear growth](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Subdifferential.lean#L333). The [Gaussian-heat, confining-flow, JKO-decrease and smooth-PDE comparisons](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L1322) concern the separate flow-construction milestones11.6–11.9, not this vector-field definition; no completion of those milestones is asserted. The [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Symmetric/Specht/Ideal/Dimension.lean#L94) has the correct object and normalization: the actual element of ℚ[Sₙ] is cₜ=aₜbₜ, and its square is (n!/f^μ)cₜ. With a left action, this ordering applies column antisymmetrization first. The proof identifies its left ideal with the same-shape polytabloid Specht module and uses the actual standard basis to determine dimension. Positivity of standardCount prevents totalized-division artefacts. The empty diagram has one standard filling and factorial one; the hook-product version gives the same scalar without division. Relabelling does not change that scalar.

New evidence resolves the earlier missing-dimension concern. [SmallDegrees, theorems four and five](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Symmetric/Specht/SmallDegrees.lean#L32), present at this exact pin, enumerate every partition via sort_parts_four/five and explicitly evaluate the hook products with norm_num. They prove the shape-indexed lists 1,3,2,3,1 and 1,4,5,6,5,4,1. [finrank_spechtModule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Symmetric/Specht/StandardBasis.lean#L391) identifies those same dimensions with standardCount, while finrank_spechtIdeal transfers them to the actual ideal used here. This is a concrete source computation, not just a proposed specialization. The squares sum to 24 and 120 respectively by integer arithmetic. It supplies the [hook-length worked criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl/README.md#L492) relevant to [Layer2 essential idempotence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl/README.md#L218). The separately specified character-row and tensor-action examples concern stronger subsequent outputs and are not assertions of this scalar identity.

Accept after completing the migration verification required by [ModularForms Layer 8](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms/README.md#L896). The source and rendered statement correctly require k≥2 and nonzero level; `CoefficientField f` is the [actual subfield of ℂ generated by positive-index Fourier coefficients](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/Fields.lean#L46), with its preferred embedding. A normalized newform is used, so rescaling by a transcendental constant cannot make this claim false.

The [argument](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/NumberField.lean#L157) establishes finite generation, not merely that every coefficient is algebraic: a finite generating set of the integral prime-Hecke algebra gives finitely many integral eigenvalues, and the finite range of the nebentypus is adjoined. Hecke recurrences then place all coefficients in that finite extension. Bad primes are included in the eigenform input. The [integrality theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/NumberField.lean#L150) passes by sorry-free source inspection. The weight-one case is correctly excluded because the modular-symbol coefficient system has degree k−2.

The definition uses `LinearMap.toMatrix` with the indecomposable-projective basis as domain and the simple-class basis as codomain. [The entry theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/CartanMatrix.lean#L147) proves Cᵢⱼ=[Pⱼ:Sᵢ], so the row/column orientation is explicit. Its coefficients are integers obtained from genuine natural composition multiplicities. Exhaustivity and pairwise nonisomorphism are hypotheses for both bases; arbitrary duplicate lists cannot silently produce a matrix of the intended map.

The chosen families share an indexing type but need not be matched by projective-cover maps. This is sufficient for the stated matrix in two selected bases; independently reordering them reorders rows and columns. It does not by itself identify the separately defined coordinate pairing with raw Hom dimension. The latter requires the projective-cover matching and the division-algebra correction described by the roadmap. The target makes no unconditional unimodularity claim; the [dual-number test](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/DualNumbers.lean#L139) computes this exact matrix as [2], as required.

New evidence closes the previously missed A₂ check: [Kronecker/A2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Kronecker/A2.lean#L78) explicitly computes the dimension vectors of the actual indecomposable projectives of the one-arrow quiver, with source-first ordering, and proves the matrix is [[1,0],[1,1]]. This is linked to the reviewed Cartan matrix by [cartanMatrix_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/CartanMatrix.lean#L147) and [the actual vertex-projective multiplicity theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Quiver/Multiplicity.lean#L140): both entries are the numbers of paths from column vertex to row vertex. Thus its columns give [P₁]=[S₁]+[S₂] and [P₂]=[S₂]. This comparison uses the real projectives and simples, rather than assigning a matrix the name Cartan.

The same [A₂ file](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Kronecker/A2.lean#L105) computes the Ringel Euler matrix [[1,-1],[0,1]], proves CᵀE=ECᵀ=I, and identifies the Ext-Euler pairing of the actual vertex simples with that matrix. These concrete computations satisfy the worked orientation and pairing check as well as the dual-number [2] check already found. The chosen order is explicitly source then target; the separate upper-triangular algebra presentation uses target-first coordinates and is not silently substituted.

The [statement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/SchurOrthogonality.lean#L108) is the first Schur orthogonality relation for the actual L² matrix coefficients of a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation. Its reciprocal dimension is legitimate because irreducibility implies a nonzero carrier. Haar probability fixes the normalization. With Mathlib's inner product conjugate-linear in the first slot, the conjugation on ⟪v₁,v₂⟫ and the order of the two vector factors are correct. Averaging a rank-one operator produces a scalar intertwiner; its preserved trace determines that scalar. The orthonormal-basis corollary also checks the four indices and Kronecker deltas.

The earlier hold demanded a separately named S₃ fixture, but the actual [roadmap criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/CompactGroups/README.md#L435) asks for reduction to the finite-group statement without new hypotheses. [inner_matrixCoeffLp_eq_inv_mul_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/Finite.lean#L481) proves the analytic-to-algebraic comparison, and [schur_orthogonality_self_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/Finite.lean#L507) executes the reduction: its proof rewrites this reviewed theorem through that comparison, installs the Borel measure structure, and supplies continuity from the discrete topology. Thus for G=Equiv.Perm(Fin3), exactly the normalized finite sum with factor 1/6 results, with no extra measure or continuity assumption. This uniform proved reduction already includes the requested example; it is stronger evidence than merely suggesting how to specialize the target. It does not assert a separately computed S₃ representation table. The circle-basis and SU(2) classification examples govern their own later outputs.
